title: Maximum Area of Two Non-Overlapping Square Submatrices
summary: Given a 2D matrix mat, find two non-overlapping square submatrices of equal size k, where each cell in the submatrices must be usable (mat[r][c] == 1).
statement: Given a 2D matrix mat, find two non-overlapping square submatrices of equal size k, where each cell in the submatrices must be usable (mat[r][c] == 1). Return the largest possible area for each square. If no such squares exist, return 0.
constraints: mat is nonempty, rectangular, binary, and has at most 500 rows and columns.
Choose two all-one square submatrices of equal side length that share no cell.
Return the area of either square, or zero if even two one-cell squares are impossible.
hints: A two-dimensional prefix sum tests whether any square contains only ones in constant time.
For a fixed side length, track the minimum and maximum row and column among valid top-left corners.
Two equal squares are disjoint exactly when their row intervals or their column intervals are disjoint, so one coordinate span of at least k is sufficient.
Feasibility is monotone as k decreases, allowing binary search for the largest side length.
editorial: Feasibility is monotone as k decreases, allowing binary search for the largest side length.

tests.explanation: Two disjoint 2-by-2 all-one squares exist, so each has area four.
The two diagonal usable cells form two disjoint side-one squares.
